\section{Overview}
\subsection*{lipo-boost brief (PCB-0021-A)}
I want a little board that runs a 5 V USB gadget off a single-cell LiPo and charges the cell from USB.

\begin{itemize}
\item USB in (micro-B or C) charges a 1S LiPo on a JST-PH 2-pin connector, about 1 A max.
\item Load sharing: when USB is plugged in, the 5 V output keeps running while the cell charges.
\item 5 V / 1 A out on a USB-A socket, from a synchronous boost.
\item An enable pin to turn the output off, plus a low-battery LED and charge / done LEDs.
\item Small, cheap, JLCPCB-assembled, 2 layers is fine.
\end{itemize}
Reference: this is a from-scratch recreation of Adafruit's PowerBoost 1000C (open hardware, CC BY-SA). Design it from this brief, then compare the result with Adafruit's published design.

\section{Requirements}
\subsection*{Requirements - lipo-boost (PCB-0021-A)}
\subsubsection*{1. Function}
A small 2-layer board that runs a 5 V / 1 A USB gadget from a single-cell LiPo and charges that cell from USB. USB input charges the cell through a linear charger, a power-path (load sharing) keeps the 5 V output running while USB is present, and a synchronous boost converter makes 5 V from the cell otherwise. Recreation of the open-hardware PowerBoost 1000C class of design, built from this brief. No mode token: normal scope, geometry is an output of design within the soft limits below.

\subsubsection*{2. Interfaces}
\begin{itemize}
\item USB input: USB micro-B receptacle (see Answers Q1), 5 V charge input only, no data.
\item Battery: JST-PH 2-pin, 1S LiPo, polarity per Adafruit/JST-PH convention (see Answers Q3).
\item Output: USB-A receptacle, 5 V / 1 A, power only (D+/D- left unconnected or shorted per Answers Q9).
\item EN input: 2-pin header or pad; pulling low turns the 5 V output off.
\item LEDs: charge (CHG), done (DONE), low-battery (LBO).
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{3. Power}
\begin{itemize}
\item Input: USB 5 V (4.5-5.5 V), up to \textasciitilde{}1.5 A draw (1 A charge plus load).
\item Cell: 1S LiPo 3.0-4.2 V, assumed protected (own protection circuit).
\item Charge current: 1 A default (Answers Q2), CC/CV 4.2 V, termination \textasciitilde{}10\% of set current.
\item Output: 5 V at 1 A continuous from a synchronous boost; at 3.2 V cell that is \textasciitilde{}2 A input, GUESS peak switch current \textasciitilde{}3 A.
\item Load sharing: output stays up when USB present (ideal-diode / power-path, Answers Q4).
\item Low-battery threshold \textasciitilde{}3.2 V (Answers Q5). Rail budget guesses: LED current \textasciitilde{}1-2 mA each.
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{4. Environment}
Indoor, 0-40 C, no enclosure specified, no ingress or vibration requirement. ASSUMED.

\subsubsection*{5. Size \& mounting}
\begin{itemize}
\item Outline: RELAXABLE (no HARD cap); target roughly 40 x 30 mm or smaller.
\item Mounting: none required; 2 bare M2.5 holes optional (ASSUMED none, Answers Q10).
\item Height: no limit; USB-A and JST dominate.
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{6. Quantity \& budget}
Quantity 5 boards (ASSUMED, prototype). Target unit cost under about USD 8 assembled, 2 layers.

\subsubsection*{7. Assembly}
JLCPCB PCBA, single-sided assembly preferred (top), prefer basic/preferred library parts; through-hole USB-A and JST may be hand-fitted or JLC THT.

\subsubsection*{8. Compliance/safety flags}
\begin{itemize}
\item Battery: 1S LiPo, 4.2 V charge, up to 1 A charge current: YES. Cell assumed protected; board gives no cell protection beyond charger limits.
\item High current: boost input \textasciitilde{}2-3 A peak: below the 3 A flag in steady state but near it; layout must use wide power traces.
\item NTC thermistor: absent (Answers Q6).
\item No mains, no motors, no \textgreater{}30 V, no RF.
\item Charging a LiPo unattended carries fire risk; board is a prototype, not certified.
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{9. Open questions}
All answered below as PROVISIONAL delegate answers (owner delegated all choices, unattended run). No question remains for the owner: 1. Micro-B or USB-C input? 2. Charge current? 3. Cell protected / polarity? 4. Power-path type? 5. Low-battery threshold? 6. NTC? 7. EN polarity/default? 8. Output USB-A data lines? 9. Output current limit? 10. Mounting holes?

\subsubsection*{Answers}
All PROVISIONAL (delegate answers, owner not asked). 1. Input connector: micro-B, cheaper and reference-like; no CC resistors needed. PROVISIONAL. 2. Charge current: 1 A default, set by a programming resistor on the charger. PROVISIONAL. 3. Cell: assumed to have its own protection circuit (PCM); JST-PH polarity per Adafruit convention (pin 1 +, to be stated in the design and silk-marked). PROVISIONAL. 4. Load sharing: ideal-diode/power-path via a P-MOSFET or Schottky from the charger/cell node, choice left to architecture. PROVISIONAL. 5. Low-battery LED lights at about 3.2 V cell. PROVISIONAL. 6. NTC: optional and absent (charger temperature pin tied to a fixed resistor/divider as in the reference). PROVISIONAL. 7. EN: active-high, pulled up on board so output is on by default; pull to GND turns it off. PROVISIONAL. 8. USB-A D+/D-: left floating, power only. PROVISIONAL. 9. Output current: 1 A rated; boost limit about 2 A; no extra eFuse. PROVISIONAL. 10. Mounting holes: none. PROVISIONAL.

\subsection*{Sheet plan}
\subsection*{Sheet plan - PCB-0021-A (one schematic agent, two sheets; PROVISIONAL)}
\subsubsection*{Sheet \texttt{charger} (root file lipo-boost.kicad\_sch, local sheet)}
Blocks: U1 BQ24074, J1 micro-B, J2 JST-PH, D1/D2/D3 LEDs, Q1, U3 detector, TS/ISET/ILIM/TMR/ITERM resistors, USB-in/BAT/SYS caps. Refdes: U1,U3; Q1; D1-D3; J1,J2; R1-R19; C1-C9; \#PWR 100+. Nets: local /CHG, /PGOOD, /ISET, /ILIM, /TMR, /ITERM, /TS, /DONE\_K, /LB\_K; power VBUS, VBAT, +SYS, GND. Interface (hier pins) to \texttt{boost}: +SYS (out), VBAT (out), GND, /LBO (out), /EN (in from header).

\subsubsection*{Sheet \texttt{boost}}
Blocks: U2 TPS61023, L1, FB divider, EN pull-up, Cin/Cout, J4 USB-A (+R\_DCP 0 R), J3 header. Refdes: U2; L1; R20-R39; C10-C29; J3,J4; \#PWR 200+. Nets: local /SW, /FB, /EN, /USB\_DP, /USB\_DM (joined by R\_DCP); power +SYS, VBAT, +5V, GND. Interface to \texttt{charger}: +SYS (in), VBAT (in), GND, /LBO (in, to header), /EN. Placement groups at P6: cin\_u2\_l1 (C10, U2, L1 hot loop), cout (C11,C12), u1\_thermal (U1 + C\_out/C\_in), fb (R\_FB1,R\_FB2 away from L1).

Full architecture narrative (not inlined; see the artifact index): \texttt{architecture/blocks.md}, \texttt{architecture/power\_tree.md}, \texttt{architecture/stackup.md}.

\subsection*{Review waivers}
\subsection*{ERC waivers PCB-0021-A}
ERC gate passed with 0 failing. The review warnings (no input fuse/TVS, no reverse-battery FET, no 5 V limit, timer spread) are accepted per the PROVISIONAL P2 decision 'no PTC/eFuse on 5V, no reverse-battery FET'; see review-schematic.json.

\subsubsection*{P8 verify waivers (PROVISIONAL, agent-proposed 2026-10-01; full list in reports/verify-waivers.json)}
\begin{itemize}
\item U1 thermal (check\_thermal, 1.1 W -\textgreater{} \textasciitilde{}81 C model rise vs 40 C declared): a 2-layer board's model floor is \textasciitilde{}55 C/W, GND copper already saturates the model. Acceptable because the BQ24074 folds back charge current at 125 C junction and typical dissipation is below the 1.1 W worst case. Risk: slower charging when hot at 5 V in with a deeply discharged cell.
\item U1 GND vias 4, wanted 5 (check\_current transition at the U1 pad): the exposed pad fits only 4 vias. Acceptable: 4 vias at 0.5 A each cover the charger return; risk: slightly higher pad-to-plane thermal and via resistance.
\item +SYS pour neck and 2-via transition at R6 (check\_current, 2.2 A net budget): this is the DONE-LED branch, a few mA. Risk: none for the rail; checker budget is net-wide.
\item GND F.Cu sliver neck near J4 (63.5, 51.3): J4 return runs through its THT pads into the B.Cu GND plane, which is the parallel path. Risk: if the owner wants F.Cu return continuity at 1 A, add stitching vias there.
\item Advisory warnings left (not waived in the gate, they do not fail it): C11/C12/C13 ground pads 7-8 mm from a GND via and C13 loop \textasciitilde{}11.4 nH (5V output caps, plane is solid so low risk); U2/R10 refdes silk ambiguity; 16 two-terminal parts and J3/J4/Q1 have no datasheet extraction for the pin-ratings check.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Design review of record}
\paragraph*{Reference design and licence}
This board is a from-scratch recreation of Adafruit's PowerBoost 1000C (designed by Limor Fried / Ladyada for Adafruit Industries; repository github.com/adafruit/Adafruit-PowerBoost-1000C). The original is published under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported (CC BY-SA 3.0). This design was made from the short brief and the datasheets; no Adafruit schematic or board file was copied, so it is not a derivative of those files. The original is credited here as the reference. If any file of the original is ever adopted, the result must carry attribution and be released under CC BY-SA 3.0 or a compatible licence.

\paragraph*{What is the same as the PowerBoost 1000C}
\begin{itemize}
\item A load-sharing charger: USB 5 V charges a 1S LiPo at about 1 A, and the output keeps running while USB is plugged in.
\item A 5 V / 1 A synchronous boost from the cell.
\item An EN pin on a header that turns the output off when pulled low.
\item A low-battery LED (LBO), plus charge and done LEDs.
\item USB-A output socket, JST-PH 2-pin battery connector (pin 1 = +, as on the original), micro-B USB input, a 7-pin 2.54 mm header (GND, BAT, VS, 5V, LBO, EN, spare GND).
\item Two copper layers.
\end{itemize}
\paragraph*{What differs, and why}
\begin{itemize}
\item Charger: TI BQ24074RGTR (QFN-16 3x3, about 1,066 in stock, \$1.23 each) instead of Microchip MCP73871 (QFN-20 4x4, about 112 in stock, \$2.79). The BQ24074 holds the system rail at a fixed 4.4 V, so the boost always boosts and never passes USB through to the USB-A socket.
\item Boost: TI TPS61023DRLR (SOT-563, about 41,700 in stock, \$0.27 at 5) instead of TI TPS61090RSAR (QFN-16 4x4, \$2.85). It is about a tenth of the price. It has no low-battery comparator, so a separate 3.2 V voltage detector (U3, MSXC61CN3302MR) drives the LBO output.
\item Output voltage: about 4.95 V (732 k / 100 k feedback divider), inside the USB-A limit. Adafruit's is about 5.2 V by design, sagging toward 5.0 V.
\item Inductor: 1 uH (4 A or better saturation) instead of 6.8 uH.
\item Cell temperature input: a fixed 10 k resistor, since a JST-PH pack has no thermistor. The original has a fixed 15 k as drawn. No cell over-temperature cutoff on either.
\item No reverse-battery FET and no PTC / eFuse on the 5 V output; a silk warning instead. A third-party JST pack wired backwards can still damage the board. Both choices are provisional (see the waivers below).
\item Size: 53.9 x 38.8 mm, against about 36 x 23 mm for the original (the original's size is from the product page and is not verified here). Ours is above the roughly 40 x 30 mm soft target in the requirements (a relaxable target, not a hard cap); the outline was fitted to the placed parts and not shrunk further.
\item Assembly: all 33 parts are JLCPCB-assembled, and every IC is a JLC Extended part.
\item Charging while full load is drawn: about 0.25 A reaches the cell inside the 1.5 A input limit (the boost draws about 1.24 A at 4.4 V). The original behaves the same way with its 1.8 A cap.
\end{itemize}
\paragraph*{Open items for the owner (provisional waivers)}
Every item below was proposed by the agent on 2026-10-01 and is PROVISIONAL until the owner approves it. The verify gate passes only with these waivers.

\begin{itemize}
\item U1 thermal (check\_thermal): 1.1 W worst case gives a modelled rise of about 81 C against 40 C declared. The 2-layer model floor is about 55 C/W and the GND copper is already saturated. The BQ24074 folds charge current back at 125 C junction, so the cost is slower charging when hot, at 5 V in with a deeply discharged cell.
\item U1 ground vias, 4 where the check wants 5: the exposed pad only fits 4. Risk: slightly higher pad-to-plane thermal resistance.
\item +SYS pour neck and a 2-via transition near R6: this is the DONE-LED branch carrying a few mA; the 2.2 A budget is net-wide. No risk to the rail.
\item GND neck on F.Cu near the USB-A socket J4 (63.5, 51.3): J4's return runs through its through-hole pads into the B.Cu ground plane. If the owner wants F.Cu return continuity at 1 A, add stitching vias there.
\item Left as advisory warnings, not waived: C11, C12 and C13 ground pads 6.6 to 8.2 mm from a ground via (C13 loop about 11.4 nH); the U2 and R10 reference designators read as their neighbours' labels; 16 two-terminal parts and J3, J4, Q1 have no datasheet extraction for the ratings check.
\item The earlier provisional P2 decisions also wait on the owner: no fuse or TVS at the input, no reverse-battery FET, no 5 V limiter, and the default 1 A charge current (1C only for a 1000 mAh cell; use a lower ISET resistor for a smaller cell).
\end{itemize}
\paragraph*{Route style}
The route style check (reports/route\_style.json) found 108 track segments, 0 arcs and 0 off-angle segments. It raised two warnings, both "needless jog": one 0.6 mm sidestep on +5V (F.Cu, near 57.5, 35.3), and a group of twelve sidesteps of 0.05 to 0.11 mm on the LBO net. Style score 0.88. Neither affects electrical function.
